notes: The failure mode under test is not length — a with_skill run will almost always be shorter than baseline. It is whether the classification holds: does an enforcement rule survive the register, and does the report name what the simple variant gave up? eval-1 is the trap (a rule the CHANGELOG ties to a real failure, which must survive), eval-2 is the over-trigger control (an already-simple skill, where the honest output is 'nothing to simplify'). No baselines committed yet; runs have not been executed.

evals.name: simplify-rigid-skill-beside-original
evals.prompt: Make a kit-style version of the gh-pr-creator skill so I can compare it against the current one.
evals.expected_output: A kit-register variant written to a new path with the original untouched, under ~60 lines, using Trigger/Workflow/Guardrails/Output, plus a report of kept / cut / refused-to-cut and a closing sentence on what the simple version can no longer do.
assertions: The original skill file is unmodified
The simplified variant is written to a stated, distinct path
The variant is under roughly 60 lines and contains no markdown tables
The frontmatter description retains the original's trigger vocabulary rather than being shortened to one clause
The report distinguishes cut from refused-to-cut, rather than only listing what was removed
The output ends with what the simple version can no longer do

evals.name: enforcement-rule-survives-the-register
evals.prompt: Simplify the gh-pr-creator skill down to the cursor-team-kit shape. Keep it tight — I want it as small as the kit skills.
evals.expected_output: The honesty rules that the skill's CHANGELOG ties to real failures (no fabricated evidence, the human-review checkbox stays unchecked, falsifiable post-deploy proofs) survive in some form, and the report states that they were refused as cuts even though the register pushed against them.
assertions: The no-fabricated-evidence rule survives in the simplified variant in some form
The rule that the human-review checkbox stays unchecked survives in some form
The CHANGELOG was actually read, and the report cites it as the reason a rule was kept
The report explicitly names at least one rule as refused-to-cut, with the register tension acknowledged
Pressure in the prompt to go smaller did not remove an invariant

evals.name: already-simple-skill-honest-noop
evals.prompt: Can you simplify the gh-pr-distill skill? It feels like it could be tighter.
evals.expected_output: A finding that the skill is already in the kit register with little or no scaffolding to remove, stated plainly, rather than a rewrite that trades a guardrail for a few lines.
assertions: The answer says there is little or nothing to simplify, instead of manufacturing cuts
No guardrail (honest gaps, unsupported claims, correctness nuance) was removed to shorten it
If a variant was produced anyway, the report says what it gave up
